subject: science
chapter_title: Nature of Matter - Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

concepts.title: Elements - Metals, Non-metals, and Metalloids
concepts.definition: An element is a pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means; elements are classified as metals, non-metals, and metalloids based on their properties.
concepts.key_idea: Elements are the simplest pure substances and are grouped into metals, non-metals, and metalloids.
question_patterns: what is an element
how are elements classified
what are metals non-metals and metalloids
give examples of metals and non-metals
what is the difference between a metal and a non-metal

solution_steps.explain: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom and cannot be split into simpler substances chemically.
Elements are divided into metals (e.g., iron, copper), non-metals (e.g., oxygen, sulphur), and metalloids (e.g., silicon, boron) based on their properties.
Metals are lustrous and conduct electricity; non-metals are dull and poor conductors; metalloids show properties intermediate between metals and non-metals.

worked_examples.question: Classify the following as metal, non-metal, or metalloid: copper, oxygen, silicon.
worked_examples.solution: Copper is a metal because it is lustrous and conducts electricity; oxygen is a non-metal as it is a gas and a poor conductor; silicon is a metalloid as it shows intermediate properties.
worked_examples.answer: Copper - metal, Oxygen - non-metal, Silicon - metalloid.

worked_examples.question: Why is silicon called a metalloid?
worked_examples.solution: Silicon has some properties of metals (lustre) and some of non-metals (brittle, semiconductor), so it is classified as a metalloid.
worked_examples.answer: Because it shows properties of both metals and non-metals.

exercises.question: What is an element? Give two examples each of metals and non-metals.
What are metalloids? Give one example.

concepts.title: Compounds - Organic and Inorganic
concepts.definition: A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio; compounds are classified as organic (carbon-based) or inorganic.
concepts.key_idea: Compounds are formed by the chemical combination of elements in a fixed proportion and have properties different from their constituents.
question_patterns: what is a compound
how is a compound different from an element
what are organic and inorganic compounds
give examples of organic and inorganic compounds
why do compounds have a fixed composition

solution_steps.explain: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio.
Organic compounds contain carbon (e.g., methane, sugar); inorganic compounds generally do not contain carbon (e.g., water, sodium chloride).
A compound has properties different from its constituent elements and its composition is always fixed by mass.

worked_examples.question: Water is a compound. Justify this statement.
worked_examples.solution: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen combined chemically in the fixed ratio 1:8 by mass, and its properties are different from hydrogen and oxygen, so it is a compound.
worked_examples.answer: Water has a fixed composition and properties different from its elements.

worked_examples.question: Classify common salt and sugar as organic or inorganic compounds.
worked_examples.solution: Common salt (NaCl) does not contain carbon, so it is inorganic; sugar contains carbon, so it is an organic compound.
worked_examples.answer: Common salt - inorganic, Sugar - organic.

exercises.question: Define a compound. How does it differ from an element?
Give two examples each of organic and inorganic compounds.

concepts.title: Mixtures - Homogeneous and Heterogeneous
concepts.definition: A mixture is formed when two or more substances are combined physically without any chemical reaction; mixtures are homogeneous when the components are uniformly distributed and heterogeneous when they are not.
concepts.key_idea: Mixtures retain the properties of their components and can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
question_patterns: what is a mixture
what are homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
give examples of homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
how is a mixture different from a compound
why do mixtures not have a fixed composition

solution_steps.explain: A mixture is obtained by mixing two or more substances physically, with no chemical reaction between them.
A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout (e.g., salt in water); a heterogeneous mixture has visibly distinct components (e.g., sand in water).
The components of a mixture retain their individual properties and the composition is not fixed, so they can be separated by physical methods.

worked_examples.question: Is a solution of salt in water homogeneous or heterogeneous? Give a reason.
worked_examples.solution: Salt dissolves uniformly in water so the composition is the same throughout, making it a homogeneous mixture.
worked_examples.answer: Homogeneous, because the salt is uniformly distributed.

worked_examples.question: Classify a mixture of oil and water as homogeneous or heterogeneous.
worked_examples.solution: Oil and water do not mix and form two visible layers, so the composition is not uniform; it is a heterogeneous mixture.
worked_examples.answer: Heterogeneous, because the components are visibly distinct.

exercises.question: Define a mixture. Give one example each of a homogeneous and a heterogeneous mixture.
Why does a mixture not have a fixed boiling point unlike a compound?

concepts.title: Separation of Mixtures
concepts.definition: The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, evaporation, distillation, sedimentation, decantation, magnetic separation, and chromatography, based on differences in their physical properties.
concepts.key_idea: Mixtures are separated using methods that exploit differences in particle size, boiling point, density, or magnetic property.
question_patterns: how can a mixture be separated
what is filtration and where is it used
how is salt obtained from sea water
explain the method of distillation
how will you separate a mixture of sand and salt

solution_steps.action: identify the components and their properties
solution_steps.explain: Determine the physical properties such as solubility, particle size, boiling point, or magnetic nature that differ between the components.
Filtration separates insoluble solids from liquids; evaporation recovers a dissolved solid; distillation separates miscible liquids by boiling point; magnetic separation removes magnetic solids.
Apply the chosen method and check that each separated component retains its original properties.

worked_examples.question: How will you separate a mixture of sand and common salt?
worked_examples.solution: Add water to dissolve the salt, filter to remove sand, then evaporate the filtrate to recover salt. Filtration separates sand and evaporation recovers salt.
worked_examples.answer: Dissolve, filter to get sand, evaporate filtrate to get salt.

worked_examples.question: How is pure water obtained from sea water?
worked_examples.solution: Sea water is heated so water evaporates, leaving salt behind; the water vapour is then condensed to obtain pure water by distillation.
worked_examples.answer: By distillation -- evaporation followed by condensation.

exercises.question: Describe how you would separate a mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder.
Explain the process of obtaining salt from sea water.

concepts.title: Differences Between Mixtures and Compounds
concepts.definition: Mixtures are formed by physical combination with variable composition and retain component properties, while compounds are formed by chemical combination in a fixed ratio with new properties.
concepts.key_idea: Mixtures are physical combinations with variable composition; compounds are chemical combinations with fixed composition.
question_patterns: how is a mixture different from a compound
state three differences between mixtures and compounds
why do compounds have a fixed composition but mixtures do not
can the components of a compound be separated by physical methods
compare mixtures and compounds with examples

solution_steps.explain: Mixtures are formed by physical mixing; compounds are formed by chemical reaction between elements.
Mixtures have variable composition; compounds always have a fixed ratio of elements by mass.
Components of a mixture retain their properties and can be separated physically; a compound has new properties and can only be separated into elements by chemical methods.

worked_examples.question: Air is a mixture but water is a compound. Justify.
worked_examples.solution: Air has variable composition and its components (oxygen, nitrogen) retain their properties and can be separated physically; water has a fixed ratio of hydrogen and oxygen (1:8 by mass) and can only be split chemically, so it is a compound.
worked_examples.answer: Air - variable composition, physical separation; Water - fixed composition, chemical separation.

worked_examples.question: Why can the components of a mixture be separated by physical means but those of a compound cannot?
worked_examples.solution: In a mixture no chemical bond forms between components, so physical methods work. In a compound the elements are chemically bonded, so only chemical reactions can separate them.
worked_examples.answer: Mixtures have no chemical bonds; compounds do.

exercises.question: Tabulate three differences between mixtures and compounds.
Why do the components of a mixture retain their original properties?

concepts.title: Symbols of Elements
concepts.definition: Each element is represented by a chemical symbol, usually the first letter or the first letter and another letter of its English or Latin name, with the first letter always capitalised.
concepts.key_idea: Symbols provide a shorthand, universal way to represent elements in chemical equations.
question_patterns: what is the symbol of an element
why are symbols used for elements
write the symbols of common elements
why is the symbol of sodium Na and not S
how are symbols of elements derived

solution_steps.explain: A symbol is the first letter (capitalised) or the first letter plus a second small letter of the element's name.
Some symbols come from Latin names, e.g., Na from Natrium (sodium), K from Kalium (potassium), Fe from Ferrum (iron).
Hydrogen is H, oxygen is O, carbon is C, copper is Cu, and gold is Au; the first letter is always a capital.

worked_examples.question: Write the chemical symbols of sodium, potassium, iron, and copper.
worked_examples.solution: Sodium is Na (from Natrium), potassium is K (from Kalium), iron is Fe (from Ferrum), and copper is Cu (from Cuprum).
worked_examples.answer: Na, K, Fe, Cu.

worked_examples.question: Why is the symbol of carbon C and not c?
worked_examples.solution: The first letter of a symbol is always written as a capital to avoid confusion with other elements; a small c could be mistaken for another element.
worked_examples.answer: The first letter of a symbol must be a capital letter.

exercises.question: Write the symbols of the following elements: hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, gold.
Why are some symbols of elements different from their English names? Give two examples.

concepts.title: Chemical Formulas of Compounds
concepts.definition: A chemical formula uses the symbols of the constituent elements along with numbers to show the exact number of atoms of each element present in one molecule of a compound.
concepts.key_idea: A chemical formula indicates both the elements present and the ratio of their atoms in a compound.
question_patterns: what is a chemical formula
how is a chemical formula written
write the formula of water and carbon dioxide
what information does a chemical formula convey
how do you write the formula of a compound from valency

solution_steps.action: identify the elements and their valencies
solution_steps.explain: Determine the symbols of the elements and their combining capacities (valencies).
Write the symbols side by side and criss-cross the valencies to get the number of atoms of each element, simplifying if needed.
Check that the total positive and negative charges balance and that the formula matches the known composition, e.g., H2O has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

worked_examples.question: Write the chemical formula of water and state what it tells us.
worked_examples.solution: Water is H2O, meaning each molecule has 2 atoms of hydrogen and 1 atom of oxygen combined chemically.
worked_examples.answer: H2O -- 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom.

worked_examples.question: Write the formula of magnesium chloride given that magnesium has valency 2 and chlorine has valency 1.
worked_examples.solution: Criss-cross the valencies: Mg gets 1 and Cl gets 2, giving MgCl2.
worked_examples.answer: MgCl2

exercises.question: Write the chemical formulas of carbon dioxide, sodium chloride, and sulphuric acid.
What information is conveyed by the formula H2SO4?

concepts.title: Properties of Metals and Non-metals
concepts.definition: Metals are generally lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors of heat and electricity, and solids at room temperature; non-metals are usually dull, brittle, poor conductors, and may be solids, liquids, or gases.
concepts.key_idea: Metals and non-metals differ in physical and chemical properties such as lustre, conductivity, malleability, and reaction with oxygen and acids.
question_patterns: what are the properties of metals
what are the properties of non-metals
how do metals differ from non-metals
why are metals good conductors of electricity
what happens when metals and non-metals react with oxygen

solution_steps.explain: Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors of heat and electricity, and mostly solid at room temperature.
Non-metals are generally dull, brittle, poor conductors, and may exist as solids, liquids, or gases at room temperature.
Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides and with acids to produce hydrogen gas; non-metals form acidic or neutral oxides and many do not react with acids.

worked_examples.question: Why are copper and aluminium used for making electrical wires?
worked_examples.solution: Both are metals and are excellent conductors of electricity, and they are ductile so they can be drawn into wires.
worked_examples.answer: Because they are good conductors and ductile.

worked_examples.question: A substance is dull in appearance and does not conduct electricity. Is it likely to be a metal or a non-metal?
worked_examples.solution: Dull appearance and poor conductivity are properties of non-metals, so the substance is likely a non-metal.
worked_examples.answer: Non-metal.

exercises.question: List three physical properties each of metals and non-metals.
What type of oxides do metals and non-metals form? Give one example each.

concepts.title: Metals, Non-metals, and Metalloids - Identification
concepts.definition: Metalloids are elements that show properties intermediate between metals and non-metals; they are used in electronics and semiconductors because of their partial conductivity.
concepts.key_idea: Metalloids bridge the gap between metals and non-metals and have intermediate, useful properties.
question_patterns: what are metalloids
give examples of metalloids
why are metalloids important in electronics
how can you identify a metalloid
state two properties that make an element a metalloid

solution_steps.explain: Metalloids are elements whose properties lie between those of metals and non-metals.
Common metalloids include silicon, boron, germanium, and arsenic.
Because they conduct electricity only under certain conditions, metalloids like silicon are used as semiconductors in electronic devices.

worked_examples.question: Why is silicon used in making computer chips?
worked_examples.solution: Silicon is a metalloid and a semiconductor, so it can control the flow of electricity, making it ideal for electronic chips.
worked_examples.answer: Because silicon is a semiconductor metalloid.

worked_examples.question: An element is lustrous but brittle and is a poor conductor. Is it a metal, non-metal, or metalloid?
worked_examples.solution: Lustre is a metallic property but brittleness and poor conductivity are non-metallic, so the element shows intermediate behaviour and is a metalloid.
worked_examples.answer: Metalloid.

exercises.question: Name two metalloids and state one use of each.
Why are metalloids called semiconductors?

concepts.title: Pure Substances and Their Classification
concepts.definition: Matter can be classified into pure substances (elements and compounds) and mixtures; pure substances have a fixed composition and definite properties, while mixtures have variable composition.
concepts.key_idea: All matter is broadly classified as pure substances (elements, compounds) or mixtures (homogeneous, heterogeneous).
question_patterns: how is matter classified
what are pure substances
what is the difference between a pure substance and a mixture
classify matter into elements compounds and mixtures
give a flowchart for the classification of matter

solution_steps.explain: Matter is first divided into pure substances and mixtures.
Pure substances are further divided into elements (cannot be broken down) and compounds (can be broken down chemically into elements).
Mixtures are divided into homogeneous mixtures (uniform composition) and heterogeneous mixtures (non-uniform composition).

worked_examples.question: Classify the following as element, compound, or mixture: gold, water, air, sodium chloride.
worked_examples.solution: Gold is an element; water and sodium chloride are compounds; air is a mixture.
worked_examples.answer: Gold - element, Water - compound, Air - mixture, Sodium chloride - compound.

worked_examples.question: Is distilled water a pure substance or a mixture? Justify.
worked_examples.solution: Distilled water has a fixed composition (H2O) and definite properties, so it is a pure substance (a compound).
worked_examples.answer: Pure substance (compound).

exercises.question: Draw a flowchart to show the classification of matter.
Classify the following as pure substances or mixtures: milk, copper, diamond, soil.
